commands.label: Java exception hierarchy and monitor probe
Compile fixed Java caller once against official provider
official Java reflection, exception contracts, monitor identity and release
candidate Java reflection, exception contracts, monitor identity and release
official canonical aliases and ordinary shadow annotations
candidate canonical aliases and ordinary shadow annotations

limitations: Canonical Throws for supported top-level, class, object, companion, interface abstract/default/override methods and public primary constructors; source/import aliases and real accessible Throwable subclasses. Supported function/constructor defaults preserve Exceptions on synthetic helpers and overloads. Throws suspend functions and secondary-constructor annotations retain explicit boundaries. Inheriting a Throws-bearing interface default requires an explicit override; generated inherited wrappers otherwise lose the Exceptions contract, so class/object/subinterface inheritance is rejected explicitly.

Canonical Synchronized on supported concrete static/instance methods and supported accessor use sites uses JVM ACC_SYNCHRONIZED. Interface/abstract members and invalid placements reject; suspend and value-class members reject as invalid; inline and default-argument combinations retain explicit unsupported boundaries.

Java caller is compiled once against official output and reused unchanged with -Xverify:all for both providers. Kotlin consumers compile against each provider separately. Signatures are compared for selected public declarations; existing unrelated interface DefaultImpls compatibility helpers are outside exact class-shape equivalence.
No new count for existing Utf8Decoder object Throws support, full Android application compatibility, or performance claim.
